question: A new cricket ball shall weigh not less than 155.9 g, nor more than _______ g, for standard conditions.
solution:
The correct answer is __**163**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• A new cricket ball used in standard conditions must weigh **not less than 155.9 grams** and **not more than 163 grams** as per the **Marylebone Cricket Club (MCC) Laws of Cricket**.
 
• The weight limit for cricket balls is crucial to maintain fairness and uniformity in the game, ensuring no undue advantage for bowlers or batsmen.
 
• These specifications are outlined in Law 4 of the MCC Laws of Cricket, which governs the dimensions and weight of a cricket ball.
 
• The diameter of a cricket ball is also regulated and should measure between **22.4 cm and 22.9 cm**.
 
• The weight and size standards apply to Test matches, One-Day Internationals (ODIs), and T20 Internationals unless specified otherwise.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Marylebone Cricket Club (MCC)**

 
 
• The MCC is the **custodian of the Laws of Cricket** and was founded in 1787.
 
• It is based at Lord's Cricket Ground in London, often referred to as the "Home of Cricket."
 
• MCC is responsible for maintaining and updating the Laws of Cricket, ensuring consistency across all formats of the game.
 
 
 
• **Cricket Ball Construction**
 
 
• A cricket ball consists of a cork core wrapped in tightly wound string, encased in a leather cover.
 
• The leather is dyed red for Test matches and white for limited-overs formats.
 
• The seam, made of six rows of stitching, plays a significant role in swing and spin bowling.
 
 
 
• **Standard Ball Usage in Matches**
 
 
• The same ball is used for 80 overs in a Test match unless it is damaged or lost.
 
• In ODIs and T20Is, a new white ball is used at the start of each innings.
 
• White balls deteriorate faster than red balls due to their coating and are harder to maintain throughout the match.
 
 
 
• **Ball Tampering**
 
 
• Ball tampering refers to the illegal alteration of the ball's condition to gain an unfair advantage.
 
• Common methods include using foreign substances, scratching the surface, or lifting the seam.
 
• It is prohibited under the ICC Code of Conduct, and offenders face penalties including suspension.
